patch.value: Baseline measured 2026-07-29 across seven source files: 89.83 line, 79.24 branch, 90.71 function. Weakest file is src/extension.ts at 61.83 line, 38.98 branch, 47.37 function; src/cli.ts branch coverage is 59.56. Thresholds are pinned at the measured floor so the number can only move up.
Enforce a real coverage gate by running tests against TypeScript sources

The package measured no coverage at all: tests imported the compiled output from dist, so the only obtainable numbers pointed at generated JavaScript offsets an author cannot act on, and no threshold was wired into any gate. The suite now runs against the TypeScript sources directly. Node executes TypeScript natively from the version floor this package already declares, so tests import source modules and the CLI subprocess tests spawn the source entrypoint, which puts the coverage report on real source lines. Enabling rewriteRelativeImportExtensions lets a source file import its siblings by TypeScript extension while tsc still emits the JavaScript specifier into dist, so the published artifact is byte-identical in shape. The gate is scripts/coverage-gate.ts: it enforces per-dimension thresholds and reconciles the reported file list against a walk of the source tree. That second check is the point. Node omits files that never load from its report entirely rather than reporting them at zero, so without it a package can satisfy a full threshold while an entire module goes unexercised.

Tests import TypeScript sources rather than dist so coverage reports on editable lines; the gate fails the build when any threshold regresses; the gate fails when a source file never loads, proven by a negative control; thresholds are recorded in package.json as a ratchet at the measured baseline; the gate runs in the release check and in CI on Node 22 and 26.
A coverage gate runs in the release check and in CI on both supported Node lines, reports against TypeScript sources, and fails when a source file is untested or a threshold regresses.

message: Add a coverage gate that reports on TypeScript sources and cannot be passed by omitting a file

patch.value: Tests moved onto TypeScript sources and scripts/coverage-gate.ts wired into release:check and CI.

npm run check passes. npm run coverage passes with 192 tests, all seven source files present in the report, at 89.83 line, 79.24 branch and 90.71 function coverage. A negative control adding an untested src file made the gate exit 1 and name that file, so the presence check is not vacuous. Thresholds pinned at 89/79/90.
Coverage gate landed and locally verified; the Node 22 CI leg is unobserved until the pull request runs.

value.text: CI measured 78.96 branch coverage where this host measured 79.24. Cause: src/release-context.ts extractOffset branches on whether a timestamp carries a UTC offset, so a host in a non-UTC zone takes a path CI does not. The gate now pins TZ=UTC when it spawns the runner, which makes the measurement identical on any machine, and the thresholds are set from that reproducible number: 89 line, 78 branch, 90 function. First concrete target for the follow-up to 100 is release-context.ts line 447.
